description.value: The study investigated neural and behavioral correlates of smoking-related action knowledge and nicotine dependence using fMRI and an orientation affordance paradigm.

spans.text: We used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and a behavioral orientation affordance paradigm to investigate the neural and behavioral correlates of automatized drug-taking actions in nicotine dependence.

value: We hypothesized that smoking-related but not control cues trigger the respective skill and action representations, which should be reflected by higher fMRI activations in smokers compared with nonsmokers in brain regions known to encode tool use skills and action knowledge.
we expected an increased behavioral responsiveness to smoking-related objects in smokers compared with nonsmokers.
action representations on both the neural and behavioral levels should correlate with the individual degree of nicotine dependence.

spans.text: We hypothesized that smoking-related but not control cues trigger the respective skill and action representations, which should be reflected by higher fMRI activations in smokers compared with nonsmokers in brain regions known to encode tool use skills and action knowledge.

description.value: The study included smokers and nonsmokers in an observational, parallel-group design. Participants underwent an fMRI experiment and a behavioral orientation affordance experiment; the fMRI study included four functional runs and one anatomical scan.

value: The two-way whole-brain RFX ANOVA revealed a significant stimulus category × group interaction, indicating differential fMRI activations across groups and object categories.

ROI-based tests showed higher fMRI activation in smokers than nonsmokers during presentation of smoking cues in regions associated with craving and reward motivation and in regions associated with skillful tool use and action knowledge.
Apparently, smoking cues automatically activate smokers' neural representations of the corresponding tool use skills and action knowledge.

value: The β weights of the GLM contrast “smoke > control” and the individual FTND scores were significantly correlated in left superior parietal lobule, posterior middle/inferior temporal and fusiform regions, right premotor cortex, middle frontal gyrus, and middle occipital gyrus.

The association between the individual level of nicotine dependence and the β values supports the assumed relationship between neural representations of drug-related action schemata and the severity of nicotine dependence.

value: The whole-brain RFX ANCOVA revealed significant correlations between the affordance index for smoking objects and fMRI cue reactivity in left premotor cortex, superior parietal lobule, middle frontal gyrus, parietal lobe, right inferior temporal cortex, and cuneus/precuneus.
This shows that automatized behavioral responsiveness to smoking-associated cues is more pronounced in heavier smokers and is related to the neural underpinnings of drug-taking skills.

spans.text: The whole-brain RFX ANCOVA with the contrast “smoke > control” and the covariate “affordance index for smoking objects” ( n = 8 smokers) ( Table 3 ) revealed left PMC ( r = 0.90, p < 0.01), SPL ( r = 0.90, p < 0.01), MFG ( r = 0.90, p < 0.01), and Brodmann area 7 in the parietal lobe ( r = 0.90, p < 0.01) as well as right ITC ( r = 0.90, p < 0.01) and a region in cuneus/precuneus ( r = 0.90, p < 0.01) ( Fig. 4 ).
